data.name: Suriname
data.summary: Suriname taxes residents on worldwide income (Wet Inkomstenbelasting 1922): dividends and interest, domestic or foreign, are taxed at progressive rates reaching 38% above SRD 234,000, with 25% Surinamese dividend tax credited. Private capital gains on securities are not among the taxable income sources. Suriname still levies a net wealth tax on residents' worldwide net assets: the consolidated law published by the tax authority states 3% of net wealth above SRD 100,000 (SRD 120,000 married), which would be very costly for this family. Inheritance tax not verified.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Worldwide income tax on dividends and interest (up to 38%); no tax on private capital gains; annual vermogensbelasting on worldwide net wealth.
regimes.eligibility: Natural persons who live in Suriname ('in Suriname wonen'), judged on the facts and circumstances (IB art. 1).

capital_gains.summary: The Income Tax Act taxes income from sources (business and work, immovable property, movable capital, periodic payments). Gains on the private sale of securities or real estate are not a listed source and are untaxed unless realised in a business. Business cessation gains can be taxed at 25% on request (art. 34(4)).

sources.title: Wet Inkomstenbelasting 1922 (geldende tekst, laatstelijk gewijzigd bij S.B. 2024 no. 3)

open_questions: No explicit statement found; conclusion drawn from the structure of IB arts. 4-7. Substantial-shareholding rules not found in the consolidated text.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Wet Inkomstenbelasting 1922 arts. 5-7 define income from immovable property, movable capital (dividends, interest) and enterprise/work; private capital gains are not included.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Gains forming part of business profits are taxed at the progressive rates up to 38%.

dividends.summary: Dividends and interest from shares, bonds and other securities are income from movable capital (art. 6), taxed in the progressive scale: 0% to SRD 108,000, then 8%, 18%, 28% and 38% above SRD 234,000 (art. 34). Surinamese companies withhold 25% dividend tax, credited against income tax (art. 52e).

sources.title: Wet Inkomstenbelasting 1922 (geldende tekst, laatstelijk gewijzigd bij S.B. 2024 no. 3)

open_questions: Unilateral relief for foreign tax on foreign dividends depends on a Staatsbesluit (art. on voorkoming dubbele belasting); not found, scored as none.
dividends.rate_basis: Art. 34(1) top rate 38% above SRD 234,000; Wet Dividendbelasting art. 5: 25% WHT, credited as a prepayment (IB art. 52e) so the total is 38%.
dividends.treaty_network: Very small network (Netherlands Kingdom arrangements; not researched).

wealth_tax.summary: Vermogensbelasting: residents are taxed on worldwide net wealth (all assets with money value minus debts; foreign assets must be declared). Art. 14: the tax is 3% of the taxable sum, being net wealth minus SRD 100,000 (unmarried) or SRD 120,000 (married). Non-residents are taxed only on Surinamese real estate and permanent-establishment assets. The tax authority still issues the 2026 return.

sources.title: Wet Vermogensbelasting 1944 (geldende tekst, laatstelijk gewijzigd bij S.B. 2002 no. 107)

open_questions: The 3% rate is as printed in the tax authority's consolidated text (last amended S.B. 2002 no. 107). A rate of 3% on net wealth is unusually high; it may be a transcription of 3 per mille. Needs confirmation from the official gazette or a Surinamese adviser before relying on it.

components.name: Vermogensbelasting (Wet Vermogensbelasting 1944, art. 14)
components.notes: Allowance SRD 120,000 for a married taxpayer (SRD 100,000 unmarried). Unilateral relief by decree possible for foreign assets taxed abroad.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Huurwaardebelasting (rental value tax) exists as a separate law; not researched.

inheritance.summary: Not verified. No inheritance or gift tax law is published on the tax authority's legislation page, and no other source could be opened. Scored as an untaxed placeholder with low confidence; treat as unknown.
open_questions: Placeholder: no inheritance/gift tax law could be verified, so the metric is treated as missing (not as untaxed).
Whether Suriname levies a successierecht/inheritance tax on residents' estates, at what rates for children, is unknown.

residency.tax_residency_test: Living in Suriname, judged on the circumstances (IB art. 1; Wet Vermogensbelasting art. 1).

corporate.summary: Income tax on bodies (lichamen) at 36% (IB art. 36). 25% dividend withholding tax.

data.us_citizen_notes: No US-Suriname income tax treaty known. US citizens remain subject to US federal tax.
open_questions: Wealth tax rate (3% vs possible 3 per mille).

succession.name: Suriname
succession.summary: Under the new Civil Code (in force May 2025 according to a summary), the legitimate portion is abolished and a surviving spouse takes control of the estate, so children have no guaranteed share but only claims limited to money. Rules on foreign law, trusts and foundations could not be sourced.
succession.family_claims: Children keep only a limited money claim once a testamentary right has been invoked; a cohabitant of at least 10 years may get a usufruct for maintenance over the home (per the Informea summary of Book 4). Details not read in the Code.
succession.foreign_law_note: No source on Suriname's conflict-of-laws rule for succession or on a choice of foreign law was found.
succession.trust_note: No trust law was found. Suriname is not a party to the Hague Trusts Convention. Foundations (stichtingen) exist in Dutch-derived law, but whether a private-benefit foundation is allowed was not sourced.
open_questions: The new Civil Code was read only via an Informea summary; verify the entry-into-force date, the abolition of the legitieme portie, and the transitional rules in the Staatsblad text.

Whether stichtingen can serve family-benefit purposes and whether any trust-like device exists was not sourced; domestic_trusts and private_foundations are 'no' because nothing was found, not because it is confirmed.
Conflict rules for succession were not found.
